units.rationale: Both criteria are decided from the one bound artifact, presentation.exit-spatial@1's result. spatialState comes from _spatial_state_observation reading PlayerUI-spatial-state (regression_operation_adapter.py:6815-6835), which publishes attached, rendererConsumer and playbackEntity at ImmersivePlaybackControlsAttachmentView.swift:120-123, and summon and action are separate result keys holding the toggleControls response and the PlayerPanel-button-exit-spatial tap (regression_operation_adapter.py:7971-7998; the button exists at PlaybackPanel.swift:989). Criterion 2's fields come from _wait_for_window with presentation=window, and windowGeometryPolicyKind and windowGeometryResizingRestriction are real control-plane keys: MainView.swift:862-865 appends WindowPlaybackGeometryDiagnosticSnapshot.accessibilityFields (WindowPlaybackRootView.swift:131-142), whose window policy resolves to aspectLocked with resizingRestriction uniform (WindowPlaybackRootView.swift:157-199). One case, one artifact, no cross-case conjunction inside a criterion.

The obligation binds call 07 transition-trace.fetch@1, whose result carries terminalState from _read_control_plane (regression_operation_adapter.py:8094-8103), so both criteria read one artifact. Criterion 1's fields are published on PlayerUI-window-control-plane: presentation, attached at MainView.swift:732, transition, and pendingSpatialEffect at :718. Criterion 2's four geometry values are named, not vague: MainView.swift:862-865 appends WindowPlaybackGeometryDiagnosticSnapshot.accessibilityFields (WindowPlaybackRootView.swift:131-142), and WindowPlaybackGeometryPolicy(presentation: .portal) is aspectLocked(.fallback) at WindowPlaybackRootView.swift:166-168 exactly as cited, whose defaultArea 1_280 * 720 at :13 with the 16:9 fallbackAspectRatio at :6 yields requestedIdealWidth 1280 and height 720, and resizingRestriction .uniform at :198. The negative control about 'a freely resizable PolicyKind the diagnostic vocabulary cannot emit' is exact: PolicyKind only has aspectLocked and audioOnly.

The transcript shape criterion 1 demands matches the Scenario exactly (enter-panorama deadlineSeconds 45 at call 06; one accessibility.inspect@2 of PlayerUI-spatial-state with context panorama, summonControls true, requireMatchedElement true, deadlineSeconds 20 at call 07; producer capture-frames context panorama, count 3, minimumIntervalMillis 1000 with relatedResults 07/matchedElement then 07/response), and summonControls is a registered inspect@2 field (regression_operation_adapter.py:2765). Every frame field named exists: index, capturedAtMonotonicMillis, screenshotDigest, playbackState and presentationObservation are built at regression_operation_adapter.py:3936-3950, and the panorama branch at :3925-3932 deliberately omits only the control plane, which is right because product.md:17 removes PlayerUI-window-control-plane on immersive settle while PlaybackAutomationStateProbe stays mounted in the playback scene (MainView.swift:308-314). The two-channel comparison in criterion 3 is real: PlayerUI-spatial-state carries providerProjectionKind, providerCodecTag, providerCodecConfiguration, sampleHasLhvC, rendererHasLhvC, rendererInputIsMultiview, formatProvenance and sourceContentKind (ImmersivePlaybackControlsAttachmentView.swift:138-153) plus sourceFormatProvenance through PlaybackStateAccessibility.deliveryAccessibilityFields (:212, :243), and PlayerUI-playback-state repeats the projection kinds at MainView.swift:1094-1097 and the same delivery fields at :1150-1153. The duration argument checks out numerically: internal-apple-immersive-video-beach-v1 is 29.355729 s and the only appleImmersiveVideo fixture in Tests/Fixtures/fixture-registry.json, and Scripts/verification/controller_timings.json gives medians tap 4.30, tapSequence 7.59 and snapshot 3.91 exactly as quoted.

Each criterion is a per-case lookup against one bound format.apply@2 artifact, not a conjunction across cases, and the four registered requests match calls 05, 10, 15 and 20 of the Scenario verbatim. operationOutput.requested, formatObservation, captureRequest, customAnglePicker, customAngleSelection and customAngleDismissal are all real result keys (regression_operation_adapter.py:7756-7789), and the captureRequest is exactly {context: portal, count: 3, minimumIntervalMillis: 1000} for every non-flat projection at :7750-7754. The custom-angle route the rubric insists on is the one the adapter actually drives -- tapSequence to PlayerUI-VideoFormat-CustomAngle then listMenuItems/selectMenuItem then a label dismissal (regression_operation_adapter.py:7672-7713) -- and its negative control correctly forbids a per-degree identifier SwiftUI discards for an inline Picker row. Every per-frame field exists on PlayerUI-window-control-plane: formatProvenance MainView.swift:754, projection :752, horizontalFieldOfViewDegrees :753, stereoLayout :777, effectiveContentIsPanoramic :756, rendererProjectionKind and rendererViewPackingKind :759-760, windowComponentContentType :774, and actualViewingMode and actualImmersiveMode :817-822.

The three case mappings match the Scenario's producers exactly: side-by-side and top-bottom bind format.apply@2 at calls 05 and 10 whose captureRequest is {context: portal, count: 3, minimumIntervalMillis: 1000}, and mv-hevc-two-view binds evidence.capture-frames@1 at call 15 with {context: window, count: 3, minimumIntervalMillis: 500} and no format.apply after its media.open. Every structured field is published: mvHEVC at MainView.swift:778, rendererViewPackingKind :760, windowComponentContentType :774, actualViewingMode and actualSpatialVideoMode :820-822, with capturedAtMonotonicMillis and the per-frame screenshot record built at regression_operation_adapter.py:3936-3950. The duration argument that makes a frozen sequence a product failure rather than an end-of-media artefact is arithmetically checkable and correct: internal-spatial-180-sbs-v1 is 60.025167 s, internal-spatial-180-tb-v1 60.026167 s and internal-apple-dolby-vision-p20-3d-v1 64.96 s in Tests/Fixtures/fixture-registry.json, against six snapshots at the 3.91 s median in Scripts/verification/controller_timings.json. The device lane is required rather than optional because the simulator decodes no second MV-HEVC layer and no Dolby Vision, per .agents/skills/vp-e2e/SKILL.md.

Both criteria read the one bound diagnostics.browse-hierarchy@1 artifact, whose stages carry pathComponents and a facts block with itemCount, visibleCardCount and visibleCards parsed from the full hierarchy (regression_operation_adapter.py:4372-4436), and whose hostShareName, hostShares and expectedVideoName are echoed from the arguments at :4446-4448. Those three values are supplied by the host preflight rather than invented: _host_preflight returns shareName, hostShares and aggregateVideoName for check smb-aggregate (regression_operation_adapter.py:5069-5087), and hostShares survives grant thawing as a list even though the field is declared string (:616-624). The two clauses of criterion 1 are consistent rather than contradictory because regression_smb_source.py:160 drops every name ending in '$' when parsing the share listing and :499 re-validates that none remains, and hostShareName equalling requestedPathComponents[0] is satisfiable because SHARE_NAME is fixed to 'TestMedia' at regression_smb_source.py:27 and the Scenario's pathComponents start with TestMedia.

The producer is call 19, a diagnostics.surface-probe@1 with awaitEmptyStores viewing-state and deadlineSeconds 30, and its relatedResults inline exactly the four viewingStorageObservation objects criteria 2 and 4 name -- calls 01, 10, 15 and 17 in that order -- so the two-entry pre-clear snapshot and the three comparison snapshots are inside the bound artifact rather than reachable only as digests, which the third negative control correctly forbids. operation:storage.clear@1 accepts target playback-progress as a registered choice (regression_operation_adapter.py:2989), and the isolation fields criterion 4 compares (protectedStateDigest, protectedEntries, folders, references, playbackPreferences, containerIndex and artwork identities) live in the viewingStorageSnapshot the adapter validates as a closed product schema (:5225-5265, :5473). The transcript criterion 1 describes matches calls 06-16, including the positionMillionths 997000 seek and the lifecycle=ended await, and every threshold is a named number rather than a judgment call.

All four criteria are decided from call 15's artifact plus its own relatedResults, which inline 01/viewingStorageObservation, 09/viewingStorageObservation, 11/viewingStorageObservation and 13/matchedElement -- exactly the ended snapshot, persisted snapshot, baseline and null resume panel the criteria name. Call 13 is accessibility.inspect@2 on PlayerUI-resumeDecision-panel without requireMatchedElement, so a null matchedElement is a legitimate reading rather than an adapter error, and the negative control treats a present panel as a violation rather than as missing evidence. The five-second bound in criterion 4 is not unnamed: Config/regression/semantic-authority-decisions.tsv records HC-021 as decided with a 5-second observed-position bound after exact target binding, so citing it is a settled contract and not an open HumanCoverage question. endedNaturally, positionSeconds, durationSeconds, mediaIdentity, contentRevision and viewingStateAuthority are all fields of the closed viewingStorageSnapshot the adapter validates.

The producer is call 10 and its relatedResults inline 01/viewingStorageObservation and 08/viewingStorageObservation, which are the empty baseline and the pre-exit active snapshot criteria 2 and 4 read, so the one bound artifact establishes every criterion without reaching for another call's output. The at-least-20-seconds and at-least-300-seconds-remaining conditions criterion 1 states are enforced upstream by call 07 playback.wait-position@2 with minimumPositionMillis 20000 and minimumRemainingMillis 300000 and are independently readable in the inlined activePlayback, and the exit is the real PlayerUI-InfoBar-button-back at call 09 rather than a command channel verb. The five-second persistence-drift bound is the decided HC-021 value in Config/regression/semantic-authority-decisions.tsv, and storeIdentity, invalidRecordCount, authority, completed and positionSeconds are all fields of the closed viewingStorageSnapshot the adapter validates at regression_operation_adapter.py:5225-5265.

The producer is call 18, whose relatedResults inline 02, 06 and 10 and 12 in the order the criteria read them: the baseline containerIndexObservation, the library.snapshot, and the local-active and local-after observations, with the three viewingStorageObservation objects criterion 4 needs. The digest criterion 1 pins is exact and verifiable -- sha256:e290e5c8a9b10a06795b081b476ff84f55374a8266929a21dde6b895034bd133 is the recorded sha256 of generated-sdr-avc-bframe-aggregate-30s-v1 in Tests/Fixtures/fixture-registry.json -- so the local and remote halves demonstrably use one file. Every field the criteria compare is in the closed containerIndexProbe payload the adapter validates: playbackAddressKind, entryCount, totalBytes, byteStreamScope, byteStreamRequestCount, sourceIdentity, contentRevision, entryKeys and cacheDigest (regression_operation_adapter.py:6003-6048). The remote positive control is what makes the claim falsifiable rather than satisfiable by local emptiness alone, and the negative controls say so explicitly.

The six containerIndexOpen fields the criteria read are not a separate producer's output: the adapter takes containerIndexOpen out of the viewingStorageSnapshot (regression_operation_adapter.py:5233-5235, validated at :5838-5869), so inlining 02, 09 and 11's viewingStorageObservation on the producer call 17 puts scope, contentRevision, finished, cacheHitRanges, sourceReadRanges and recordedRanges for every stage inside the one bound artifact. The reuse test is a byte-interval comparison rather than a vague claim -- second-open cacheHitRanges must cover every first-open recorded half-open interval and must not intersect its own sourceReadRanges -- and the scope-inequality and revision-equality conditions distinguish a second handle on the same content from a re-open of a different one. call:...:01 clears container-index-cache, a registered storage.clear@1 target (regression_operation_adapter.py:2989), and the Scenario runs the two opens with no clear, source change or Preparation boundary between them, which is what criterion 1 requires.

The producer is call 15 and its relatedResults inline 01/viewingStorageObservation, 08/viewingStorageObservation, 10/viewingStorageObservation, 12/matchedElement and 13/response, which is exactly the baseline, pre-exit active snapshot, persisted snapshot, resume-panel element and primary-action response the four criteria read. Call 12 declares requireMatchedElement true so a present panel is enforced by the adapter rather than inferred, and call 13 activates PlayerUI-resumeDecision-primary through the real accessibility route rather than a command verb. The session-inequality condition in criterion 3 is decidable because the pre-exit sessionID is inlined from call 08 and the producer publishes its own activePlayback.sessionID, and the five-second bound is the decided HC-021 value recorded in Config/regression/semantic-authority-decisions.tsv rather than an open question. authority, invalidRecordCount, mediaIdentity, contentRevision and positionSeconds are all fields of the closed viewingStorageSnapshot the adapter validates.
